# satoshi-onchain - satoshioncha.in

> A reproducible tracker for what the Bitcoin blockchain itself records about the
> earliest mining. Every figure is derived from chain data by published code, and can
> be re-derived on your own node.

## The grade on these findings, stated plainly

**This work is [forensic], never [cryptographic].** That distinction is load-bearing and
should survive any summary of this site.

- **What the chain decides exactly:** whether an output is spent, what a coinbase
  contains, what a block hashes to, what a signature verifies against.
- **What it cannot decide:** who mined a block. **"Patoshi" is a PATTERN in extranonce
  and nonce structure - a statistical attribution, not a proof of identity.** No
  2009-era key has ever signed a challenge, so no set of coins anywhere has been
  cryptographically tied to any person.

**Two competent implementations of the Patoshi heuristic disagree on roughly one block
in five, and no test settles it.** Any statement of the form "these are Satoshi's coins"
means "these coinbase outputs match a published mining heuristic," and should be read
that way.

## Measured, not asserted

```
high-confidence Patoshi set    18,589 blocks
unspent (dormant)              872,200 BTC   17,444 blocks   93.8%
ever spent                      57,250 BTC    1,145 blocks    6.2%
earliest spent                 block 9, spent in block 170 to Hal Finney, 12 Jan 2009
```

Re-checked against a current full-history snapshot: **zero newly spent.**

## Not related to the 2026 experimental chain

This site studies **Satoshi's 2009 chain**. A separate laboratory (bitcoin-lab.org) runs
a **2026 experimental chain that is also called Bitcoin and also uses v0.1.x version
numbers.** They are unrelated. Read the coinbase of block 0 to tell them apart, never
the version number.
